title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
Symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure-generation code, laboratory design studies, and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. The repository supports the companion studies of the FLRW and Vaidya sectors and of the conformal Kerr (Thakurta-Kerr) sector.

1.7.1 - the tau-branch drift is weighted by conformal time. A correction release: one error in the adiabatic closed form of the proper-time branch, found in a re-check of the manuscript against its own convention, and the verification built to catch it.

The tau-branch drift was weighted by the wrong clock. The conformal factor runs with the conformal time, A = A(η), so the first-order drift of the charges along an orbit is weighted by the conformal time elapsed along that orbit, on both branches. On the t-branch that is the branch clock. On the tau-branch it is not: the proper time τ(r) is the clock that functional measures and sets the timing, but it is not the slow variable. The closed form had been built with τ(r) as the weight, and the energy part of the first-order coefficient came out 46% low at the published parameters.

The drift clock has a closed form. Along the tau-orbit, dη/dr = [E r³ - 2MaJ r D_E/Δ]/√S: a second-kind part with vector b = (-2MaJ(E²-1), 0, 0, E, 0) plus a third-kind part at Δ = 0 with numerator -2MaJ[2ME²r - (E²-1)a²]. At a = 0 it reduces to the Schwarzschild coordinate time E r³/√S, the bulk part of the Vaidya advanced-time clock of Paper I. The weight-two assembly acquires the corresponding horizon term.

The new check is built to fail on the old answer. verify_tau_branch_drift_clock.py derives the clock symbolically, compares it with 1/H_pr along the η-parametrised Hamiltonian flow (agreement to 1e-13 at three parameter sets), and requires the proper-time density to be rejected by the same comparison (it misses by 34-46%). It then closes the weight-two assembly, horizon part included, against the direct double integral to 1.4e-13, for the energy source and for the full Euler source. The earlier checks had passed because the identity they test holds for any weight.

What did not change. The validation against the true non-autonomous flow had used the η-parametrised Hamiltonian throughout, so its slopes (2.12 ± 0.03) and the content digest are unchanged; nothing on the t-branch changes, nor do the frozen closed forms, separatrices or classification. The horizon part is verified by quadrature; its closed form in Fay theta-ratios is not derived in this release.

Archive. Thirty-one manifest entries, each mapped to one command and one checksum; twenty-three Wolfram Language and ten Python verification scripts. Content digest 42ed5ab1779c5813.
